title: yabai.toml
description: The configuration file of yabai, read by the daemon at startup and on each reload.

daemon.description: Settings of the daemon itself: the file watch and the scripting addition load.

auto_reload.description: Reload the file when it is saved, as config --reload does.

load_scripting_addition.description: Load the scripting addition at startup, after each Dock restart, and when a reload turns this on, with sudo -n.

config.description: One key for each option of yabai -m config, under the option's name.

debug_output.description: Enable output of debug information to stdout.

mouse_follows_focus.description: When focusing a window, put the mouse at its center.

focus_follows_mouse.description: Automatically focus the window under the mouse.

display_arrangement_order.description: Specify how displays are ordered (determined by center point).

builtin_display_last.description: Order the built-in display after all other displays.

window_origin_display.description: Specify which display a newly created window should be managed in.

window_opacity_duration.description: Duration of transition between active / normal opacity.

window_animation_easing.description: Easing function to use for window animations.

menubar_opacity.description: Changes the transparency of the macOS menubar.

insert_feedback_color.description: Color of the window --insert message and mouse_drag selection.

window_border.description: Draw a border around each window, in the active color for the focused window and in the normal color otherwise.

window_border_width.description: Width of the window border in points.

window_border_hide_single.description: Hide the border while a tiled window is alone on its space.

active_window_border_color.description: Color of the border of the focused window.

normal_window_border_color.description: Color of the border of every other window.

tab_bar.description: Draw a tab bar on top of every tabbed container, like the tabbed layout of i3.

tab_bar_height.description: Height of the tab bar in points.

tab_bar_offset.description: Space in points between the bottom of the tab bar and the windows of the container, inside the backdrop card if there is one.

tab_bar_backdrop.description: Backdrop card of the 'glass' tab bar style.

tab_bar_backdrop_color.description: Optional tint of the backdrop card.

tab_bar_card_padding.description: Space in points between the edges of the backdrop card and the tab bar and windows inside it.

tab_bar_window_radius.description: Corner radius in points that windows are assumed to have.

tab_bar_font.description: Font of the tab titles, e.g. 'Menlo:12'.

tab_bar_icons.description: Draw the application icon left of the title in each window tab.

tab_bar_focused_color.description: Background and text color of the active tab of the tabbed container that holds the focused window.

tab_bar_focused_text_color.description: Background and text color of the active tab of the tabbed container that holds the focused window.

tab_bar_inactive_color.description: Background and text color of the active tab of every other tabbed container.

tab_bar_inactive_text_color.description: Background and text color of the active tab of every other tabbed container.

tab_bar_unfocused_color.description: Background and text color of the tabs that are not active.

tab_bar_unfocused_text_color.description: Background and text color of the tabs that are not active.

top_padding.description: Padding added at the upper side of the selected space.

bottom_padding.description: Padding added at the lower side of the selected space.

left_padding.description: Padding added at the left side of the selected space.

right_padding.description: Padding added at the right side of the selected space.

window_gap.description: Size of the gap that separates windows for the selected space.

layout.description: Set the layout of the selected space.

auto_padding.description: Remove padding on 'tree' spaces that hold at most one tiled container, so that it fills the whole area of the display (the menu bar, Dock and 'external_bar' are still respected).

tree_default_orientation.description: Orientation of an empty 'tree' space when its first window opens, like i3's 'default_orientation'.

tree_autotiling.description: Like the i3 autotiling script: a new window that opens next to a window splits that window along its longer side, so the space is divided like a binary tree.

focus_wrapping.description: What window --focus 'north|east|south|west' does at the edge of a 'tree' space, like i3's 'focus_wrapping'.

mouse_modifier.description: Keyboard modifier used for moving and resizing windows.

mouse_drop_action.description: Action performed when a managed window is dropped in the center of some other managed window: swap the two windows, or make the dropped window a tab of the other one.

mouse_drop_preview.description: What a managed window dragged over another managed window shows where it would be dropped.

mouse_drag_split.description: Dragging with the left button, without the 'mouse_modifier' key, on the gap between two tiled windows resizes their split: the gap follows the pointer, and each child keeps its minimum share.

external_bar.description: Specify top and bottom padding for a potential custom bar that you may be running.

skip_window_focus_animation.description: Bypass macOS space animation when an application or window on an inactive space is focused.

space_layout.description: Keep a fixed number of spaces on each display.

scratchpad_exclusive.description: Keep at most one scratchpad window shown.

scratchpad_raise.description: When window --toggle '<LABEL>' acts on a scratchpad that is shown on the active space but does not have focus, focus and raise it instead of hiding it.

scratchpad_below.description: Put scratchpad windows on the same stacking sub-layer as tiled windows instead of above them, so focusing a tiled window brings it in front of a shown scratchpad.

scratchpad_grid.description: Set the frame of a scratchpad window, as with window --grid, each time window --toggle '<LABEL>' shows it while it was hidden.

space.description: One table for each space that has a label, a pin or its own options.

index.description: The Mission Control index of the space, from 1.

label.description: The label of the space, as with space --label.

pin.description: The display that the space is pinned to, as with space --pin.

top_padding.description: Padding added at the upper side of the selected space.

bottom_padding.description: Padding added at the lower side of the selected space.

left_padding.description: Padding added at the left side of the selected space.

right_padding.description: Padding added at the right side of the selected space.

window_gap.description: Size of the gap that separates windows for the selected space.

layout.description: Set the layout of the selected space.

auto_padding.description: Remove padding on 'tree' spaces that hold at most one tiled container, so that it fills the whole area of the display (the menu bar, Dock and 'external_bar' are still respected).

rule.description: One table for each rule, with the keys of rule --add.

label.description: Label used to identify the rule with a unique name.

insert.description: Place a new window as window --insert does.

grid.description: Set window frame based on a self-defined grid.

manage.description: Window should be managed (tile vs float).

mouse_follows_focus.description: When focusing the window, put the mouse at its center.

sub-layer.description: Window is ordered within the given stacking sub-layer.

native-fullscreen.description: Window should enter native macOS fullscreen mode.

scratchpad.description: Unique identifier used to identify a window scratchpad.

one_shot.description: Apply the rule once and remove it (rule --add --one-shot).

signal.description: One table for each signal, with the keys of signal --add.

label.description: Label used to identify the signal with a unique name.

active.description: Filter on the active or focused state, yes or no in signal --add.

event.description: The event that triggers the signal.
